title: Driving for Work
osha_standards: OSH Act Section 5(a)(1) General Duty Clause
summary: Driving for work is risky. Wear your seat belt, stay focused, stay rested and sober, secure your loads, and drive a well-maintained vehicle.
talking_points: Wear your seat belt. Seat belts are the single most effective means of reducing deaths and serious injuries in traffic crashes.
Distracted driving is a factor in 25 to 30 percent of all traffic crashes. Drivers make more than 200 decisions every mile. When driving for work, safe driving is your primary responsibility.

Drowsy driving may be involved in more than 100,000 crashes each year. If you are tired, stop. A short nap (15 to 45 minutes) and caffeine can help temporarily. Get out of the car every 2 hours to stretch and walk briskly.
Warning signs of fatigue: you cannot remember the last few miles, you drift from your lane or hit a rumble strip, you yawn repeatedly, or you tailgate.

Alcohol, certain prescription and over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs reduce alertness, coordination, and reaction time. Alcohol is a factor in 39 percent of work-related traffic crashes. Avoid medications that cause drowsiness.
Avoid aggressive driving such as excessive speed, tailgating, failing to signal, running red lights, and passing on the right. Do not engage other drivers, and let others merge.
Secure tools and equipment in transit. Loose objects can slide or become airborne in a crash, so store them outside the passenger compartment.
Vehicles should be on a routine preventive maintenance schedule, and a mechanic should inspect each one at least annually.
site_hazards_to_check: Loose tools or materials in the passenger compartment
Vehicles with overdue maintenance or inspection
Phones, food, or other distractions in the cab
Long drives with no planned rest stops
Workers who took medication that causes drowsiness
discussion_questions: What distracts you when you drive for work, and how can you remove it?
What are the warning signs of fatigue, and what will you do when you notice them?
How do we secure tools and materials in our trucks?

flags: All stats and advice quote-accurate to OSHA Guidelines for Employers to Reduce Motor Vehicle Crashes: seat belts most effective, 25-30% distracted, 200+ decisions/mile, 100,000 drowsy crashes, 15-45 min nap, 2-hour breaks, fatigue signs, 39% work-related crashes alcohol, aggressive driving list, secure loads, annual mechanic inspection.
Citation: General Duty Clause 5(a)(1) is the correct hook (OSHA has no driving standard); it is not a 1926 section and is the honest mapping. Talk makes no legal commitment.
Non-blocking: statistics come from a 2004-era guide and are dated; consider refreshing with current NHTSA/NIOSH figures. Attribution: osha.gov, public domain. No UK wording.
